Middle East.headline: 'The last thing you expect': Locals near UK airbase react to 'terrorist act' arrests
Middle East.body: British police were questioning five men on Monday on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences after they were detained near an air base that has been used by the US to strike Iran. Residents of a village that's situated under a mile away from the base were ordered to evacuate on Sunday as the investigation continues, with many left taken aback by the developments.

Americas.body: Hurricane Nolo is moving away from Hawaiian islands but threat of heavy rain, flash floods and strong winds persists Hurricane Nolo was moving away from the Hawaiian islands on Sunday, but the threat of heavy rain, flash flooding and strong winds persisted in areas of the island chain still recovering from previous storms. Nolo was about 365 miles (585km) south-south-west of Honolulu and moving away from the Big Island at about 12mph (19km/h). But the Hawaii county civil defense agency said a high wind warning, wind advisory and high surf advisory remained in effect for parts of the island through Sunday evening as Nolo’s maximum sustained winds rose to 115mph. Africa.headline: DRC — Ebola outbreak surpasses 8,000 cases amid regional spread and mpox detection
Africa.body: The ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 8,000 confirmed cases and 3,901 deaths, establishing it as the largest and deadliest epidemic in the country's history. Caused by the Bundibugyo strain, transmission has expanded to 63 health zones across seven provinces, including new cases in Bulu and Dungu near the South Sudan border. Humanitarian response efforts, contact tracing, and containment remain heavily constrained by persistent conflict and civilian displacement. Furthermore, the detection of an mpox case in Ituri province threatens to further overburden the country's healthcare system.

Africa.headline: Somalia — Acute hunger and child malnutrition risk worsening due to projected El Niño floods
Africa.body: Millions of people in Somalia continue to endure high levels of food insecurity as acute malnutrition among children is projected to deteriorate further. According to warnings from the Federal Government of Somalia and the United Nations, anticipated El Niño-driven heavy flooding between October and December 2026 threatens to exacerbate humanitarian conditions. The deteriorating outlook is compounded by severe funding shortfalls, risking widespread operational disruptions in aid delivery across affected regions.

Asia-Pacific.headline: At least 33 people killed in western Myanmar airstrike, rebel group and aid worker say
Asia-Pacific.body: Sept 28 (Reuters) - Dozens of people were killed in a Myanmar military airstrike on Monday near a market in the country’s war-torn Rakhine state, which borders Bangladesh, according to a rebel group that controls the area and a local aid worker. • At least 33 people have died and 36 were injured in the airstrike in the town of Kyauktaw in Rakhine state, according to the Arakan Army, a rebel group fighting the military. • The number of victims was confirmed by aid worker Wai Hun Aung, who has a team operating in the area.

Asia-Pacific.body: 33 killed, 36 injured after Myanmar military airstrike in war-torn Rakhine A military airstrike near a market in Kyauktaw killed at least 33 people and injured 36 others. The strike hit an area said to be far from the frontline as fighting and air raids intensify across Myanmar. A military airstrike near a market in Myanmar's war-torn Rakhine state killed at least 33 people and left 36 others injured, according to the Arakan Army and a local aid worker cited by Reuters. The strike took place on Monday in Kyauktaw, a riverside town in northern Rakhine that is controlled by the Arakan Army, an ethnic armed group fighting Myanmar's military. Asia-Pacific.headline: Death toll rises as floods hit Thailand and Myanmar
Asia-Pacific.body: BANGKOK: Heavy rain has killed eight people in Thailand since mid-September, the government said on Monday, as Bangkok battled flooding for a fourth straight day. At least eight more people have been confirmed dead in neighboring Myanmar. According to Thailand's Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation, the deaths occurred in three eastern provinces since Sept 16, with none reported in the capital. More than 500,000 households and 1.7 million people in 27 provinces are currently affected by floods after an intense weather system hit the region, the department said. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: NCoS Contains Cholera Outbreak at Kano Custodial Centre
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: The Nigerian Correctional Service (NCoS) says it has brought a recent cholera outbreak at the Kurmawa Medium Security Custodial Centre in Kano State under control. The service said the outbreak was confirmed through laboratory investigations conducted on Sept. 23 by its medical team in collaboration with Kano State public health authorities. In a statement, the Service Public Relations Officer, Jane Osuji, said the Controller-General of Corrections, Sylvester Nwakuche, was immediately briefed and directed that necessary measures be sustained to protect the health and welfare of inmates and personnel. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Hurricane Polo’s moisture could lead to major flooding in the Southwest
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Hurricane Polo will bring a flood threat, damaging winds and high seas to Baja California and parts of Mexico Monday, and then the tropical moisture from Polo will carry into the southwestern U.S. and could trigger major flooding across the region. Where is Polo now? Right now, Polo is located about than 125 miles west of Cabo San Lazaro, Mexico, and has sustained winds of 115 mph. The storm will make landfall Monday afternoon along the Baja California coast, producing as much as a foot of rainfall and triggering flash flooding and mudslides across the region.
